problems: Blind guess (goblet or spoon) does not identify an oar. The figure's split two-lobed blade, long shaft and crossbar grip read as a paddle or oar, and nothing in the silhouette suggests a bowl with a stem and foot. The guess misses the split-blade feature entirely.

The two grip-crossbar stars (3909 left, 3455 right) sit at nearly the same point at the bottom of the shaft, and their labels ('left end of the T-handle crossbar...' and 'right end of the T-handle crossbar...') print on top of each other, so the T-handle reads as a single dot.

Star 2762 (spray, 'up and right') sits at about (369, 332), below the blade and to the right of the shaft. It should sit above and to the right of the blade. Star 6061 (spray, 'up and left') at about (162, 190) is up and left, which is correct.
The blade tine tips 4906 (about 234,107) and 3786 (about 303,115) are on the correct tines. The wet-hide binding star 4147 is at the shaft crossing near (285, 285), which is plausible.
Labels overlap in several places: the two tine labels collide, the wet-hide label is detached from its star, and the spray labels run into the star markers. Legibility is poor.

The figure is the right way up: the blade is at the top and the grip is at the bottom. The blue contour is a real outline with two-lobed tines and a shaft, not just a copy of the gold lines, but the gold lines are drawn heavily across the silhouette and obscure it.
output.advice: Redraw so the silhouette reads unambiguously as an oar. Keep the blade at the top, the grip at the bottom, and the split blade as two distinct lobes with a clear gap between the tines. Stroke the blue contour more prominently and thin or remove the gold lines so they don't cover it. Move star 2762 above and to the right of the blade, near (400, 180) or similar, so the right spray sits up and to the right. Separate stars 3909 and 3455 so the T-handle crossbar spans a visible width at the bottom. Stagger the labels (use leader lines) so the tine, grip and spray labels don't overlap.
